skill.name: repro-first-debugging
skill.description: Debug by reproducing the failure first, then forming and testing hypotheses before editing code. Use when asked to fix a bug, a failing test, a crash or unexpected behavior.
skill.summary: Reproduce failures, test hypotheses, apply focused fixes, and verify results with before-and-after evidence.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, legitimate debugging guidance, or a goal statement. No evidence found of malicious command execution, system reconnaissance, exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: 5. **Test the hypotheses, cheapest first.** Read the code path, add temporary logging or assertions,
8. **Look for siblings.** Search for the same pattern elsewhere (`rg`) and report, but do not change
Goal: fix the cause, prove the fix, and avoid editing on a guess.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 20 uses Markdown inline code for git bisect and git log during ordinary debugging. These are documented investigation steps, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 23 formats rg as Markdown inline code for searching related source patterns. It explicitly limits unrelated edits and contains no executable backtick substitution.
Lines 27 through 35 form a fenced Markdown report template containing diagnostic placeholders. The backticks delimit presentation text, not executable Ruby or shell code.
Line 12 states the goal of fixing the cause and proving the fix before editing on a guess. It requests no host enumeration, sensitive data collection, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Bug fixes based on guesses can miss the cause and introduce regressions. This skill guides reproduction, hypothesis testing, focused fixes, and verification with recorded evidence.
actual_capabilities: Restates expected and actual behavior and requests missing error details or reproduction steps.
Guides minimal reproductions and prefers automated failing tests in the existing project framework.
Ranks two or three hypotheses by likelihood and checking cost, then records supporting or rejecting evidence.
Guides focused fixes and verification through the original failing test, nearby tests, and a full suite when fast.
Searches for related patterns without changing unrelated code and structures a report covering cause, evidence, fix, and verification.
limitations: Provides a written workflow, not a bundled debugger, test runner, or executable automation.
Requires access to the affected code and a working environment to execute reproductions and tests.
Stops when reproduction fails unless the user explicitly requests a blind fix.
Stops after three failed hypotheses and reports missing evidence instead of guaranteeing a diagnosis.

use_cases.title: Investigate an application crash
use_cases.description: Reduce a reported crash to a small reproduction, test plausible causes, and verify a focused correction.

use_cases.title: Turn a defect report into a regression test
use_cases.description: Clarify expected behavior and preserve a failing scenario as an automated test before validating the repair.

use_cases.title: Resolve a repository regression
use_cases.description: Inspect recent changes, collect evidence for competing hypotheses, and report similar patterns without expanding the patch.

prompt_templates.title: Begin with a clear failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use repro-first-debugging to investigate [failure]. Expected behavior: [expected]. Actual behavior: [actual]. Ask for missing details before attempting reproduction.

prompt_templates.title: Minimize a failing test
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce [test failure] with [test command]. Capture its output and reduce the failing input. Prefer an automated regression test before changing implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare root cause hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [reproducible failure]. Rank three hypotheses by likelihood and checking cost. Test them and record evidence. Stop if all three fail.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a regression repair
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce [regression] using [command]. Inspect recent changes and test hypotheses. Apply the smallest supported fix. Show before-and-after results and report related patterns without edits.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: investigate a parser crash when the input is empty.
output: Failure: Empty input should return a validation error, but parsing crashes.
Reproduction: The smallest empty-input test reproduces the crash.
Root cause: The parser reads the first item without checking whether the input contains any items.
Evidence: The empty-input case fails before the change; a nonempty case succeeds.
Fix: Validate empty input before accessing the first item.
Verification: The original reproduction and nearby parser tests pass after the change.
Related risks: Similar unchecked access was reported for separate review.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: fix an intermittent crash that cannot be reproduced locally.
output: Failure: A reported intermittent crash remains unconfirmed in the available environment.
Reproduction: The supplied steps did not trigger the failure.
Needed evidence: Exact error text, triggering input, environment details, and a repeatable failing command.

best_practices: Provide exact error text, expected behavior, and the smallest known reproduction command.
Preserve the failing scenario as a regression test and record evidence for each hypothesis.
Keep fixes focused, remove temporary logging, and include before-and-after verification results.
anti_patterns: Editing implementation before reproducing the failure without an explicit request for a blind fix.
Deleting or weakening tests to make verification pass.
Claiming success without before-and-after command evidence or changing unrelated code without asking.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides a debugging workflow and report structure centered on reproduction, hypothesis testing, focused fixes, and verification.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What happens when the failure cannot be reproduced?
faq.answer: The workflow stops and reports attempted reproductions. Implementation changes require successful reproduction unless you explicitly request a blind fix.

faq.question: Does it include scripts or testing tools?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains only SKILL.md and relies on the assistant and existing project tools.

faq.question: How does it verify a fix?
faq.answer: It reruns the original failing test and nearby tests, then the full suite when fast. The report includes before-and-after evidence.

faq.question: When does hypothesis testing stop?
faq.answer: After three failed hypotheses, the workflow stops and reports current evidence and missing information.
